notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-442dc5 (issue #1458). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in it.

Provenance. All three recorded artifacts were re-downloaded and all three hashes match byte for byte: the arXiv v2 PDF b2338ef1...b3594038, the v2 e-print 30968bad...4b91878ac (bms2.tex, 3266 lines) and the open-access published PDF on Centre Mersenne 6b43d1ff...23ff23dd. The findings were checked in both texts, which mattered: two of them (E10, E11) are phrased in the published text and were verified there.

Numbering and coverage. Sixteen environments share one per-section counter. Simulating that independently gives 173 numbered objects, exactly the extraction's count, and every one of them is covered once locator ranges are expanded - the locators use forms like 'Lemmas 4.15-4.17' and 'Lemmas 4.25-4.27', which a naive matcher reads as two numbers rather than three. Before expanding them I had Lemma 4.16 (closure of quasisyntomic and quasismooth maps under composition and base change) and Lemma 4.26 (the finite-free/flat injectivity criterion) as apparent gaps; both are in fact cited, and Lemma 4.16's content is folded into the statement of the quasisyntomic-site item. After expansion the only uncovered objects are four introductory remarks, all commentary: the forward reference to the prismatic site, the extension to TR^r, Schneider's sheaves, and the comparison with BMS1.

Statuses. The single library item cites WittVector, PreTilt and WittVector.fontaineTheta, all of which exist at Mathlib 082e2d3 (RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52, RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634 and RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165, the last inside namespace WittVector). The 56 planned items cite 22 layers, all of which exist in data/atlas.json.

Routes. Twelve source routes and one Part II, all accepted. Every source route's stage exists and belongs to the roadmap that claims it. The Part II is exemplary: it adds one item to a roadmap that two other extractions already propose with the same parent, rather than opening a competing one.

Mistakes in the paper. All 12 were checked at their locators and all 12 are confirmed; all are misprints affecting nothing. Several are settled by the paper against itself - d_R against the d_S of the next sentence (E9), D(C) against the D(S) of the same sentence (E2), gr^n TC(A)[-2i] against the introduction's consistent n (E5), and the missing relative base in gr^0(TC^-(A)[1/u]) against Proposition 11.15 and its own proof (E12). Two were settled by computation rather than comparison: E7, where the display's isomorphism p^{i-1-n}V degenerates exactly at n = i - 1, and E10, where f = μ^j g and μ = ξφ^{-1}(μ) give g - ξ^{i-j}φ^{-1}(g) ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}, not the printed μ^{i-j}.

Nothing was corrected in place. Verdict: accept.
